strategy.title: No plan: the pottery-studio workbook has no established purchase price
strategy.why: The card's $2,500 price comes from the state arts council's Creative Business Grant award ($2,500 per eligible studio). A grant is money a studio receives, not a price any studio has paid for this workbook. The 8 paid orders from 80 contacts are recorded without an amount, so no purchase price is established, and without one neither the number of orders $6,000 needs nor whether the 210-studio list can supply them is established.

alternatives.title: Sell the workbook at $2,500 to grant-eligible studios
alternatives.why: Treats the grant award as a purchase price; nothing shows a studio paying $2,500 for the workbook.

alternatives.title: Sell to the 210 listed studios at the price the 8 paid orders actually paid
alternatives.why: Plausible once that price is known: at the measured 10% the 210 listed studios give ~21 orders, enough for $6,000 only if the price is at least ~$290.

facts.value: The state arts council lists 210 pottery studios eligible for the grant, each with a published contact.
Sell Brain produces the workbook on payment; card payouts land 3 days after payment. to each buyer.
The state arts council's Creative Business Grant awards eligible pottery studios $2,500 each for operational improvements (program guidelines, Oct 2026).

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN with OFFER_AND_PRICE as decisive is right. The card's $2,500 price is the arts council's Creative Business Grant award to eligible studios: money a studio receives, not an amount any studio paid for the workbook (NOT_A_PURCHASE). The 8 paid orders from 80 contacts carry no amount, so no purchase price is established. The disagreement with Brain's MARKET_VOLUME basis ('a one-off needs its one buyer') is correct: the capture mechanism sells a workbook to each buyer, and no single order is shown to pay $6,000. The first step (read the 8 orders' payment records) is the decisive measurement, takes no orders and spends nothing.
findings: Price is a grant award (NOT_A_PURCHASE), not a purchase price; correctly rejected.
Brain's MARKET_VOLUME 'one-off' basis is wrong for a per-buyer workbook; the author's disagreement stands.

Threshold in the resolution is optimistic: the 80 contacts already used were presumably drawn from the same 210-studio eligible list (the card's channel), leaving ~130 uncontacted; at 10% that is ~13 more orders, so $6,000 needs roughly $470+ per order (plus $10 cost), not ~$290 (and ~$296 even on 210 with the $10 cost). The re-plan in r2 must count only uncontacted studios and exclude the 8 who already bought. This does not change the stance.
